$comment: The single source for every colour, measurement and typeface the Grid Point
Code applications use. build-tokens.mjs turns this file into the stylesheet
the website imports, and into the resource files an Android app would.
Edit here and regenerate. Nothing downstream is written by hand, and CI
fails if a generated file has drifted from this one.
Hex values are literal on both themes rather than one theme plus opacities:
a translucent colour has to be composited against whatever sits behind it,
which is a different answer on every surface and an extra layer on Android.

colour.$comment: Named for what they are, not where they are used. The roles are below.

role.$comment: What each colour means, so a new screen does not have to guess.

$comment: One tint per level of the code, coarsest first. Prussian stepped into the
ground in ten equal parts, so depth reads as weight and the eye starts
where the world does. The ramp inverts on the dark theme: level one is
brightest there, and level ten sinks into the page.
'ink' is the type colour that stays legible on each tint. It changes at
level six on both themes, which is also where the parity state resets.
The ramp steps evenly in sRGB -- and it has one wider step, between
levels five and six, which is where the ink changes. That step is
deliberate. A tint can be too light for the light ink and too dark for
the dark one at the same time, and the band where both fail is real:
0.18 to 0.23 of luminance on the light theme, 0.14 to 0.21 on the dark.
An even ten-step ramp has to cross that band, and whichever level lands
inside it cannot carry normal-size text at 4.5:1 whatever ink it is
given. So the crossing is made in one stride rather than landing in it:
the steps stay even within each ink group, and the group boundary jumps
the band. Every level now clears 4.5:1 against its own ink, the worst
being 4.66.
Levels one and ten are unchanged: they anchor the identity, and the
respacing happens between them.
Found by axe on /typos, where an 11px label sat on level five and six
tints and measured 3.16 to 4.42.
Which colour fills each role of Material's colour scheme, for the Android
application. Every value names a colour above, or a level as 'level-N'
and its ink as 'level-N-ink'; none is a hex of its own, so there is still
exactly one place a colour is decided.
Material asks for about thirty roles and the palette has twelve colours,
so some roles share one. That is deliberate rather than a gap: a
container of prussian is the pale end of the level ramp, because the
ramp already is prussian stepped into the ground, and brass is never a
fill at all. It is the ink codes are set in, so its container is the
surface it is always printed on.
The outline is ink-soft rather than a rule. Material draws a text field's
border with it, and a border that shows where to type has to reach 3:1
against the surface; the rules are decoration and do not.
build-tokens.mjs checks every pairing here before it writes anything:
4.5:1 for anything that carries type, 3:1 for the outline. The first
draft put brass on the sunken tint and measured 4.38.

space.$comment: Eight steps, each roughly 1.5 times the one before it.

radius.$comment: A survey instrument has square corners. A pill only ever carries state.

$comment: One frame for the whole site. The masthead, every page and the footer
share it, so a reader moving between pages sees text begin in the same
place rather than jump sideways. Before this there were five widths and
the heading on one page started 189px further in than on another.
It is the FRAME and not the line. Prose inside it stays capped at the
measure above, which is what keeps a paragraph readable in a wide one.
All three are under the SIL Open Font Licence and all three are served
from this origin. A font content delivery network would put a third
party between the reader and a page whose entire claim is that it needs
nobody.
IBM Plex Mono was chosen by measuring it. The alphabet has no O, I, S,
Z or B in it, so the confusions every typeface guide leads with cannot
occur in a code at all; what is left is eight pairs, and the pair that
decides between candidate faces is C against G.
No slashed-zero feature is set because the zero is already dotted.
Letter spacing keeps ten characters from touching at small sizes.
